label: FY2027 Q2 (Jul–Sep 2026)
headline: Data center revenue doubles and quarterly orders top $1B, yet the stock is 60% below June: after the spin-off Modine is a pure data center cooling company, and the market is waiting for margins

points.b: A fourth straight quarter of record orders
points.t: Data center orders topped $1B in the quarter, more than twice this quarter's revenue, including a $400M program from a hyperscale customer.
Data center gross margin fell from 24.4% to 19.7%: material, component and tariff costs rose, and it paid more to lock in supply.
On 1 Oct it spun off vehicle and genset thermal management into Gentherm; the new full-year outlook covers only data centers and commercial HVAC: revenue $3.1–3.2B, +50–55%.

reaction: Stock: closed at $123.34 before the report (2 Nov), against a $296.82 closing high on 2 Jun. That period includes the 1 Oct spin-off (shareholders also received Gentherm shares), so part of the decline is value that was distributed; we haven't separated it. The call is on the morning of 4 Nov; after-hours and next-day data to be added. We found no reliable consensus for this quarter, so comparisons are to a year ago; a GuruFocus headline says revenue and adjusted EPS beat estimates.

segments.title: Revenue mix
segments.take: Over 80% of the increase came from data centers; commercial HVAC is also supplying coils to data center customers; the spun-off Performance Technologies barely grew.

rows.why: Mainly chillers, air handling units and white-space equipment for North American hyperscalers. Operating profit $61.2M (+70%); adjusted EBITDA margin 15.4% against 18.1% a year ago, though better than last quarter. A third dedicated data center plant in Calgary started production.
Coils (many sold to data center customers), anti-corrosion coatings (+28%) and heating and ventilation products. Adjusted EBITDA margin 15.1%, flat with a year ago.
Genset and commercial vehicle demand grew while automotive and off-highway fell. No longer part of Modine from 1 Oct.

segments.note: Shares are of the $1.013B segment total; the gap to consolidated revenue of $994.4M is intersegment eliminations.

extras.title: Where it sits in the AI loop
extras.take: Modine's job in the loop is getting heat out of the data center: the hotter the GPU racks, the more and bigger the chillers and air handlers. It sells large cooling equipment outside and inside the data hall, competing with Vertiv, Schneider, Johnson Controls and Carrier.

items.w: Orders were more than twice this quarter's data center revenue, and backlog is a record. A hyperscaler signed a $400M program, a sign Modine is on the core supplier list.
North American chiller lines go from 13 to 20 (by March 2027). Chiller sales fell this quarter on shipment timing; the company expects a sharp rise in the second half.
To secure supply it signed long-term agreements with key suppliers at higher prices, on top of tariffs and raw materials. The company says it is recovering this through pricing.

Liquid cooling takes some heat straight off the chip, but it still has to be rejected outdoors by chillers and dry coolers. Wider adoption changes the equipment mix and doesn't necessarily shrink Modine's market.
Expansion capex and inventory built for orders made first-half free cash flow negative, and net debt rose from $363M to $574M.

extras.title: Where growth comes from
extras.take: After the spin-off Modine is mainly a data center cooling company: data centers are already about 60% of continuing revenue. Growth depends on capacity; profit on whether costs can be passed on.

items.w: Four straight quarters of record orders, with backlog enough to support second-half growth; the full-year continuing revenue outlook is +50–55%.
The company expects data center earnings to grow more than 80% for the year, based on better fixed-cost absorption as lines ramp, plus pricing.

items.b: A second line through commercial HVAC
items.w: Commercial HVAC is also a tier-two coil supplier to data center customers and newly qualified to supply evaporators.
Long-term revenue and earnings targets come at the 18 Nov analyst day, and we'll review the zone then.
Hyperscalers delaying projects; data center construction hitting local opposition or power limits; costs that can't be passed on; new lines ramping poorly.

trends.why: +35% in five quarters; excludes Performance Technologies from next quarter
Dipped in Q1 on expansion costs, recovered in Q2
Q1 grew 44%, far faster than EBITDA's 5%; the two measures differ

valuation.take: About 15 times EV/EBITDA on the full-year continuing-operations outlook, and about 21 times trailing adjusted EPS (including the spun-off business). Not a high multiple, because margins are falling, cash flow is negative, and the post-spin basis won't be clear until the analyst day.

debt $724M − cash $151M (30 Sep, before the spin-off)

forward.title: FY2027 for continuing operations
steps: Less about $60M of D&A and $35M of interest, 25% tax, 53M shares
forward.note: The company gives no continuing-operations EPS; D&A, interest and tax are our assumptions. The spin-off's effect on debt shows in next quarter's statements.

scenarios.note: Bear: data center orders slow in FY28 and cost pressure persists; base: 20 lines running full with margins back to a year ago; bull: further expansion and more hyperscale programs. Price = (EBITDA × multiple − $570M net debt) ÷ 53M shares. These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

pricezone.sub: FY29 EBITDA × our EV/EBITDA; price at the 2 Nov close (the day before the report)
pricezone.why: The price is inside the zone: buying at $123, the base case gains about 74% and the bear case loses about 26%, a reward/risk of about 2.8, among the best in this batch. At the $130 top of the zone the reward/risk is about 2.2; at the $105 low end, about 7.8. But these are profits two and a half years out, with a capacity ramp and cost pass-through in between; we'll review the zone after the 18 Nov analyst day sets long-term targets.

history.title: Against its own past 5 years
history.sub: P/S (TTM revenue, including the spun-off business), quarter ends
history.note: About 1.8x now, equal to the five-year median and less than half the 4.1x of end-June. Five years ago it was mainly an auto parts company at 0.3x; the data center business lifted the valuation several times over. Revenue shrinks after the spin-off; on continuing operations the P/S is about 2.1x. We calculate it from SEC quarterly revenue, diluted shares and quarter-end closes.

cash.title: Adjusted EBITDA
cash.note: First-half free cash flow was −$146M: data center expansion capex and inventory built to meet orders. Restructuring, spin-off and similar cash payments totaled $27.7M.

valuation.next: The 18 Nov analyst day brings long-term targets; the next report is around early February 2027, with Performance Technologies shown as discontinued operations.

changes.before: Component shortages caused production inefficiencies last quarter.
changes.now: Long-term agreements with several strategic suppliers; supply has stabilized, at higher cost.
A third plant in Calgary (air handling units) in production; 13 chiller lines, 20 by year-end.
Plans to rename itself Modexus Solutions, with a shareholder vote on 13 Nov.
